 Judgment

This is petitioners' appeal filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ('the Act' for short)
seeking enhancement of compensation granted for the death of Sajidali S/o Sikandar Bagawan in a motor vehicles accident dated 05.01.2017.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
3. Petitioners are the parents, wife, children and sister of deceased-Sajidali Bagwan.
It is the case of the petitioners' that on 05.01.2017, the said deceased-Sajidali and one Rasheed were proceeding on motorcycle bearing Reg.No.MH-02-FA-6380 (for short 'motorcycle').
It was driven by Rasheed.

At about 5:00 p.m., when they reached Tongarali village, a lorry bearing Reg.No.MH-18-AA-9726 Sri. Sikandar And Ors vs Sri. Sandesh And Anr on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38369018/
2 ('offending vehicle' for short), being driven by its driver in a high speed, in a rash or negligent manner came from the opposite side and dashed against the motorcycle.

entities.text: Sri. Sikandar And Ors vs Sri. Sandesh And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Due to impact, both deceased and Rasheed sustained injuries and were declared as brought dead by the hospital.
As the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation.
4. Respondent No.1 remained ex parte.
5. Respondent No.2 has filed written statement denying that accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
It has also disputed the age, occupation, income of the deceased and that petitioners were dependents on him.
The compensation claimed is highly exorbitant and sought for dismissal of petition.
6. Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal framed necessary issues.
7. In respect of death of Rasheed, his parents filed MVC No.281/2018.
the Tribunal has clubbed both cases and led common evidence.
8. Petitioner No.1 (in MVC No.280/2018) is examined as PW.1, Yunus who is petitioner No.1 of MVC No.281/2018 is examined as PW.2.

They have relied upon Exs.P1 to 15.
9.
Respondents have not led any oral or documentary evidence.

10. Vide the impugned judgment and award the Tribunal has partly allowed the petition and quantified the compensation at Rs.12,22,000/- with interest at 6% per annum and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same.

The details of the compensation granted are as under:
 Sl. Head Amount  No. awarded in Rs.
 1. Loss of dependency 11,52,000/-
 2. Loss of love and affection 40,000/-

3 . Funeral expenses 15,000/-
 4. Towards loss of estate 15,000/-
11. Respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award.
12. During the course of arguments, learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the notional income at Rs.8000/- considered by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
The Tribunal has not granted any compensation towards loss of future prospects.
The interest granted at 6% is on the lower side and prays to allow the appeal.
13. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and award and prays to dismiss the appeal.

sentences.text: Heard arguments and perused the records.

15. Having regard to the fact that respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award, the findings of the Tribunal that accident occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle and in the said accident deceased sustained injuries and died and also that petitioners are dependents on him has attained finality.
16. Based on the record, the Tribunal has rightly taken the age of deceased as 35 years and '16' as the multiplier.
In the absence of proof of income the Tribunal is justified in considering the income on notional basis.
Since the accident is of the year 2017, the notional income ought to have been taken at Rs.10,250/-.
The Tribunal has not granted any compensation towards loss of future prospects.

Since deceased was aged less than 40 years, 40% of income is required is to be added towards loss of future prospects as per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1 (Magma's case), 40% of Rs.10,250/- is Rs.4,100/-.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1 (Magma's case)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, income is required to be taken at Rs.14,350/-.
Petitioner No.6 being the sister of deceased is not dependent on him.
Leaving her, there are five dependents.
Therefore, 1/4th is required to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses and remaining 3/4th is to be taken into consideration for calculating loss of dependency.
With these components the loss of dependency is Rs.14,350x12x16x3/4=Rs.20,66,400/- as against Rs.11,52,000/- granted by the Tribunal.

17. As per the decision of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others2 (Pranay Sethi's case) and Magma case, the (2018) 18 SCC 130 (2017) 16 SCC 680 petitioners 1 to 5 being the parents, wife and children are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.40,000/- each i.e.
Rs.2,00,000/- under the head loss of consortium and compensation in a sum of Rs.40,000/-
granted under the head loss of love and affection is disallowed.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others2 (Pranay Sethi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
18. As per the decision in Pranay Sethi's and Magma cases, the Tribunal has rightly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.15,000/- each under the head loss to estate and funeral expenses (which includes transportation of dead body).
19.

Thus, in all petitioners are entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.22,96,400/- as against Rs.12,22,000/- granted by the Tribunal with interest at 6% per annum as detailed below:
Sl. Heads Amount awarded by Amount awarded No the Tribunal by this Court 1. Loss of dependency Rs.11,52,000/- Rs.20,66,400 2. Loss of consortium Rs.40,000/- Rs.2,00,000/-
(loss of love and affection)
3. Funeral expenses Rs.15,000/- Rs.15,000/-

4 4. Loss to estate Rs.15,000/- Rs.15,000/-
Total Rs.12,22,000/- Rs.22,96,400/-
20.

To this extent, the impugned judgment and award is required to be modified and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
(i) Appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) Appellants/petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.22,96,400/-
as against Rs.12,22,000/- granted by the Tribunal with interest at 6% per annum.

(iii) Respondent No.2/insurance company shall deposit the compensation amount together with interest at 6% p.a. within a period of six weeks from the date of this order (minus the compensation already paid/deposited).
(iv) Registry is directed to send a copy of this order to the Tribunal.
